answer: A decaying identity bond prices bulk forgery out. Each newcomer locks 60 credits in a crystal-clear bond that melts each epoch, so idle fakes cannot sit free. Honest agents wander through work, earning fees that refill the bond, while a whisper of activity triggers spot-checks on suspects. Forging 1,000 identities costs 1,000 x 60 = 60,000 credits plus 5,000 upkeep, so a fake army burns 65,000 in one epoch while an honest agent pays 60 once.
